text: Such as are thy habitual thoughts, such also will be the character of thy mind; for the soul is dyed by the thoughts.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: The universe is transformation: life is opinion.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: If thou art pained by any external thing, it is not this thing that disturbs thee, but thy own judgement about it. And it is in thy power to wipe out this judgement now.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: Since it is possible that thou mayest depart from life this very moment, regulate every act and thought accordingly.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: In the morning when thou risest unwillingly, let this thought be present: I am rising to the work of a human being.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: No longer talk at all about the kind of man that a good man ought to be, but be such.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: Do not act as if thou wert going to live ten thousand years. Death hangs over thee. While thou livest, while it is in thy power, be good.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: Look within. Within is the fountain of good, and it will ever bubble up, if thou wilt ever dig.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: Be like the promontory against which the waves continually break, but it stands firm and tames the fury of the water around it.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: The best way of avenging thyself is not to become like the wrong doer.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: Remember that every man lives only this present time, which is an indivisible point, and that all the rest of his life is either past or it is uncertain.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: I have often wondered how it is that every man loves himself more than all the rest of men, but yet sets less value on his own opinion of himself than on the opinion of others.

text: Do not disturb thyself by thinking of the whole of thy life.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: Occupy thyself with few things, says the philosopher, if thou wouldst be tranquil.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: The perfection of moral character consists in this, in passing every day as the last, and in being neither violently excited nor torpid nor playing the hypocrite.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: When thou wishest to delight thyself, think of the virtues of those who live with thee.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: Remember how long thou hast been putting off these things.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: Hold every hour in your grasp. Lay hold of to-day's task, and you will not need to depend so much upon to-morrow's.

text: While we are postponing, life speeds by.
author: Seneca

text: Everywhere means nowhere.
author: Seneca

text: It is not the man who has too little, but the man who craves more, that is poor.
author: Seneca

text: If you live according to nature, you will never be poor; if you live according to opinion, you will never be rich.
author: Seneca

text: Men learn while they teach.
author: Seneca

text: We suffer more often in imagination than in reality.
author: Seneca

text: When a man does not know what harbour he is making for, no wind is the right wind.
author: Seneca

text: I feel, my dear Lucilius, that I am being not only reformed, but transformed.
author: Seneca

text: You need a change of soul rather than a change of climate.
author: Seneca

text: Every day, therefore, should be regulated as if it closed the series, as if it rounded out and completed our existence.

text: Our motto, as you know, is to live according to Nature.

text: There are things which are within our power, and there are things which are beyond our power.
author: Epictetus

text: Men are disturbed not by things, but by the principles and notions which they form concerning things.
author: Epictetus

text: Demand not that events should happen as you wish; but wish them to happen as they do happen, and you will go on well.
author: Epictetus

text: If you wish to improve, be content to appear foolish and stupid with respect to externals.
author: Epictetus

text: Never proclaim yourself a philosopher, nor make much talk among the ignorant about your principles, but show them by actions.
author: Epictetus

text: No great thing is created suddenly, any more than a bunch of grapes or a fig. If you tell me that you desire a fig, I answer you that there must be time. Let it flower first, then bear fruit, then ripen.
author: Epictetus

text: Every habit and faculty is maintained and increased by the corresponding actions: the habit of walking by walking, the habit of running by running.
author: Epictetus

text: If you would make anything a habit, do it; if you would not make it a habit, do not do it, but accustom yourself to do something else in place of it.
author: Epictetus

text: We become just by doing just acts, temperate by doing temperate acts, brave by doing brave acts.
author: Aristotle

text: For one swallow does not make a summer, nor does one day; and so too one day, or a short time, does not make a man blessed and happy.
author: Aristotle

text: It makes no small difference, then, whether we form habits of one kind or of another from our very youth; it makes a very great difference, or rather all the difference.
author: Aristotle

text: Habit is thus the enormous fly-wheel of society, its most precious conservative agent.
author: William James
source: The Principles of Psychology, ch. IV "Habit"

text: Never suffer an exception to occur till the new habit is securely rooted in your life.
author: William James
source: The Principles of Psychology, ch. IV "Habit"

text: Seize the very first possible opportunity to act on every resolution you make.
author: William James
source: The Principles of Psychology, ch. IV "Habit"

text: Keep the faculty of effort alive in you by a little gratuitous exercise every day.
author: William James
source: The Principles of Psychology, ch. IV "Habit"

text: We are spinning our own fates, good or evil, and never to be undone.
author: William James
source: The Principles of Psychology, ch. IV "Habit"

text: Could the young but realize how soon they will become mere walking bundles of habits, they would give more heed to their conduct while in the plastic state.
author: William James
source: The Principles of Psychology, ch. IV "Habit"

text: I went to the woods because I wished to live deliberately, to front only the essential facts of life, and see if I could not learn what it had to teach, and not, when I came to die, discover that I had not lived.
author: Henry David Thoreau
reference: Where I Lived, and What I Lived For

text: Our life is frittered away by detail. Simplify, simplify.
author: Henry David Thoreau
reference: Where I Lived, and What I Lived For

text: Time is but the stream I go a-fishing in.
author: Henry David Thoreau
reference: Where I Lived, and What I Lived For

text: If one advances confidently in the direction of his dreams, and endeavors to live the life which he has imagined, he will meet with a success unexpected in common hours.
author: Henry David Thoreau

text: If you have built castles in the air, your work need not be lost; that is where they should be. Now put the foundations under them.
author: Henry David Thoreau

text: As if you could kill time without injuring eternity.
author: Henry David Thoreau

text: Trust thyself: every heart vibrates to that iron string.

text: Nothing can bring you peace but yourself.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

text: Write it on your heart that every day is the best day in the year.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

text: The journey of a thousand li commenced with a single step.

text: By nature, men are nearly alike; by practice, they get to be wide apart.
author: Confucius

text: The prosecution of learning may be compared to what may happen in raising a mound. If there want but one basket of earth to complete the work, and I stop, the stopping is my own work.

text: If you add only a little to a little and do this often, soon that little will become great.
